title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Keepalive Payload Architecture
purpose: Define the configured payload policy for automatic WebSocket keepalive ping frames on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels.
design_summary: `Http3ServerOptions.WebSocketKeepAlivePayload` lets the server owner configure a static ping payload for automatic keepalive frames. The server validates the payload against the RFC 6455 control-frame 125-byte limit at startup, copies it into server-owned storage, and passes it to the existing keepalive scheduler for each automatic ping.
data_and_state_considerations: The payload is immutable from the server's perspective after listener creation because the server copies the configured memory. The scheduler remains disabled unless a positive keepalive interval is configured, and WebSocket writes still flow through the tunnel context write gate.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The default payload remains empty to preserve existing behavior.
Payloads larger than 125 bytes are rejected before the listener is exposed to callers.
Dynamic per-ping payload selection remains outside this static payload policy.
risks: Application-specific liveness semantics still need to choose payload contents carefully because peers are allowed to echo pong payloads.
External WebSocket-over-H3 peer behavior still needs live interoperability proof before promoting beyond local loopback evidence.
